strings.name: Jean-Laurent Bonnafé
strings.role: Director and CEO of BNP Paribas
strings.summary: Jean-Laurent Bonnafé is a French banking executive who joined BNP in 1993 after engineering studies and public-sector work. He helped integrate the group and managed retail banking. Appointed BNP Paribas CEO in 2011, he has overseen business disposals and asset-management expansion while responding to major compliance incidents at the bank.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through November 17, 2026. Group and subsidiary roles, director and chair, and transaction announcements and closings are distinguished; the bank's legal liability does not constitute a personal conviction.
strings.influence.rationale: A long-standing leader of BNP Paribas, involved in European banking and global corporate finance.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education and early career
strings.facts.f1.value: Graduated from École Polytechnique and École des Mines with engineering training, and worked in the French public sector early in his career.
strings.facts.f2.label: Governance role
strings.facts.f2.value: Director and CEO of BNP Paribas; Jean Lemierre is board chair, a separate role.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Business portfolio changes
strings.highlights.h1.text: The group sold Bank of the West and acquired AXA Investment Managers through Cardif, reshaping its retail-banking and asset-management portfolio.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Response to compliance failures
strings.highlights.h2.text: After the bank reached a sanctions-related plea and penalty agreement with US authorities in 2014, he publicly expressed regret and outlined corrective measures.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Third-quarter results commentary published
strings.timeline.t1.text: The release records his remarks as CEO after the board meeting on the 27th and reports progress on integrating AXA Investment Managers.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Cardif completes AXA Investment Managers acquisition
strings.timeline.t2.text: The group's insurance subsidiary completed the transaction and established a long-term asset-management partnership with AXA.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Bank of the West sale completed
strings.timeline.t3.text: The group closed the sale to BMO and subsequently announced cross-border commercial cooperation; this was not an exit from all US business.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Bank reaches US sanctions agreement
strings.timeline.t4.text: The bank agreed to plead guilty and pay about US$8.9 billion; Bonnafé responded on July 2. This is not recorded as a personal conviction.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Appointed group CEO
strings.timeline.t5.text: The BNP Paribas board appointed him chief executive officer, a role distinct from board chair.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Becomes Fortis Bank CEO
strings.timeline.t6.text: He oversaw retail-banking integration and held the role until February 1, 2011.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Becomes managing director of BNL
strings.timeline.t7.text: He took on management responsibilities at BNL after its integration into the group.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Joins BNP
strings.timeline.t8.text: He entered banking after French public-sector work, later overseeing strategy and merger integration.
